target_customer: Developers and users of Ethereum payments needing scalable transactions
problem: Ethereum had low transaction throughput; Elph built Plasma sidechains for high throughput payments.
business_model: payments infrastructure (blockchain network); no revenue model found

founders.name: Abhinav Lanka
founders.background_notes: Named in Brex announcement, not on YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Plasma sidechains on Ethereum were immature and demanded blockchain scaling expertise; claim of 6,000 transfers per second came from the company.

defensibility.rationale: Open protocols and rival scaling approaches meant no structural moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Brex acquired the team in March 2019 without disclosed terms.

market_need_then: Ethereum congestion limited payments; no dated demand data was read beyond company posts.

brand_strength.rationale: Short lived brand acquired within months of the batch; no press on the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Elph, a five person Winter 2019 team that had previously sold Streem to Box in 2014, was acquired by Brex in March 2019 shortly after the batch. Terms were undisclosed, and Brex framed the founders as supporting its product roadmap, which suggests an acquihire style outcome rather than a product outcome. Its blockchain payments network did not continue as an independent business per sources found.
notes: CB Insights lists 880K raised, seen on one aggregator and unverified, so no rounds recorded. YC describes Elph as digital payments infrastructure; Brex and Crunchbase describe blockchain Plasma sidechains. Success factor strong_team_execution is a weak inference from a repeat founder team; failure factor acquihire_soft_landing is plausible but not stated by a source, so omitted. Founding year inferred from batch; not sourced.
